text: 4. [3:440] Sexual Harassment Claims: Claims against an employer for sexual harassment are subject to the following coverage analysis under CGL policies: a. [3:441] No “bodily injury liability” coverage: There is no CGL “bodily injury” coverage for claims of sexual harassment for the following reasons: (1) [3:442] Often no “bodily injury”: Sexual harassment claims typically seek damages for emotional distress, mental anguish, etc. Most courts hold emotional distress does not constitute “bodily injury” under a CGL policy (¶ 3:356). [See Aim Ins. Co. v. Culcasi (1991) 229 CA3d 209, 220, 280 CR 766, 772] ➪ [3:443] PRACTICE POINTER FOR EMPLOYER'S COUNSEL: If you represent the employer, utilize discovery to determine whether the employee complains of physical symptoms (such as ulcers, headaches, rashes) resulting from emotional distress. (2) [3:444] No accidental “occurrence”: More fundamentally, CGL policies cover only accidental “occurrences” (see ¶ 3:357); and by its very nature, sexual harassment is intentional, not accidental. [See David Kleis, Inc. v. Sup.Ct. (California Ins. Co.) (1995) 37 CA4th 1035, 1047-1048, 44 CR2d 181, 188-189] b. [3:445] Coverage under CGL “personal injury liability” coverage?
